Many of these platforms host a wide range of harmful content, including video tutorials that explain how to launch cyberattacks or use cybercrime tools. On YouTube, such tutorials are often uploaded by creators with thousands of followers and attract even larger audiences. Because many of these videos can be followed with only basic technical skills, they make cybercrime accessible to a broad audience and may serve as a pathway into cybercrime, particularly among youth. As part of a broader effort to prevent cybercrime through awareness and influence campaigns, law enforcement agencies and researchers have collaborated to counter the potential impact of these tutorials. In this study, we partnered with the Cyber Offender Prevention Squad (COPS) of the Netherlands Police to deploy a series of YouTube video advertising campaigns targeting tutorials related to two forms of entry-level cybercrime: distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks and remote access trojans (RATs). We examine the engagement generated by these campaigns among the target audience, focusing on when and where engagement occurred, who was exposed to the ads, what exposed users were searching for, and which ads performed best. The results indicate that DDoS-related ads generated higher levels of engagement than RAT-related ads, while socialization-based messages achieved greater audience retention than deterrence-based messages. Analysis of the target audience (18-24 years old) further showed that the vast majority of users who viewed and engaged with the ads were estimated to be non-parents, with males comprising most of this group. These findings provide valuable insights for law enforcement agencies considering the use of online advertising campaigns as a cybercrime prevention strategy.

articles.title: Shared Answers, Different Paths: Gender and University Plans among Japanese Adolescents
articles.authors: Yuko Nozaki
articles.abstract: Educational expectations are often compared by gender as if shared responses denoted shared goals. Using Japan’s Longitudinal Survey of Newborns in the 21st Century, I examine 10,227 adolescents who selected a university plan in grade 9, when the questionnaire offered no separate junior college option. I classify their grade 10–12 reports by whether a four-year university plan was maintained or which alternative was first named, and decompose the gender gap in four-year university entry at ages 19–20. Boys’ entry exceeded girls’ by 3.01 percentage points. The composition component rises from 0.88 points under a binary classification to 2.77 under three categories and 3.09 under five. Girls more often named junior college or college of technology; a majority of them later entered junior colleges. Without identifying when intentions formed, the results show how aggregating response categories can make gendered postsecondary pathways look like unequal realization of shared plans.

articles.title: Willing or not: how older adults in Chile respond to the obligation to go online
articles.authors: Manuel Torres-Sahli; María Fernanda Cerda-Díez
articles.abstract: Forced digitalisation, the withdrawal or downgrading of offline channels, makes going online an obligation that many older adults do not experience as a choice. During the lockdowns, family contact also required going online. Research on proxy internet use and non-use shows that many older adults meet this obligation through others, but says little about how their stance towards it relates to their use, or how that relation varies across situations. We classify how older adults respond to that obligation. We draw on 44 interviews with older adults at day centres in Chile's Metropolitan Region, analysed thematically and coded by episode: one response to the obligation in one situation. Responses vary along two analytically independent dimensions: endorsement, the stance a person takes towards the obligation, and engagement, whether they use technology alone, through others or not at all, and how far beyond the required task. Delegation was the commonest response. Two further results stand out. First, stance and use come apart: several participants who are resigned to the obligation use technology extensively, while a few who accept it go no further than the required task. Second, the same person takes different stances depending on what the technology is for: most participants express more than one, pursuing the channel that reaches their family while leaving the state procedure to a relative or declining it. A simpler grouping by overall stated stance gives three profiles, Proactive users, Resigned users and Resisters, which match how participants describe themselves but hide this variation. Whereas social gerontology explains digital inequality and non-use through skill, use and help, the study adds the stance a person takes towards the obligation. Reluctant use and non-use can be reasoned positions, and treating them as skill deficits misrecognises them. Skills provision should therefore be paired with offline channels of equivalent quality.

articles.title: The Pressure to Appear Fine: Emotional Suppression, School Belonging, and Psychological Well-Being among High School Students
articles.authors: Ha Phuong Khanh; Ngan Thi Thuy Nguyen
articles.abstract: Many adolescents answer “I’m fine” when they are not. This study examined the associations among school belonging, the pressure to appear fine, expressive suppression and psychological well-being in Vietnamese high school students, including whether suppression mediates the link between the pressure and well-being and whether the pressure mediates the link between belonging and suppression. Students in grades 10 to 12 completed an online questionnaire in September and October 2026, and 120 valid responses were analysed with partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). The measurement model met the criteria for reliability and validity. Two of the eight hypotheses were supported: the pressure to appear fine was strongly associated with expressive suppression (β = 0.684, p < 0.001), and school belonging with psychological well-being (β = 0.581, p < 0.001). Belonging was not significantly associated with the pressure or with suppression, neither the pressure nor suppression was significantly associated with well-being, and no indirect path was significant. In this sample, the expectation of looking composed is closely tied to how students manage emotional expression, whereas school belonging is the factor most clearly associated with how well they feel.

articles.title: Evaluating a university micro-placement programme in England: A convergent mixed-methods study of student experiences, attainment and progression
articles.authors: Isobel Kane; Paulo Ricardo Vieira Braga; Katie Tyrrell; Brandon Harris
articles.abstract:
Work-integrated learning is associated with improved academic and employment outcomes. However, access to traditional placements remains uneven. Micro-placements offer shorter, paid and potentially more accessible work experience, but evidence concerning their longer-term outcomes is limited. This study evaluated an English university programme in which students completed up to 30 hours of paid work within university teams.
A convergent mixed-methods design combined institutional outcome data with 10 semi-structured interviews. Propensity-score matching and doubly robust augmented inverse probability weighting estimated adjusted associations between participation and two outcomes: degree attainment and employment or further-study status 15 months after graduation. Interview transcripts were analysed separately using Template Analysis.
Qualitative findings indicated that micro-placements supported confidence, workplace awareness, transferable skills, professional networking, and career clarity. Students particularly valued the programme’s flexibility, paid nature, and supportive university environment. However, perceived benefits depended on the relevance, challenge, and quality of placements, alongside opportunities for reflection. Quantitative analyses found no statistically significant association between participation and attainment. An unexpected negative association with progression was observed, although this finding was based on a small sample and remained vulnerable to selection bias and unmeasured confounding.
The findings suggest that micro-placements constitute a valuable and flexible developmental intervention, but that participation alone may be insufficient to improve attainment and progression outcomes without high-quality placement design and structured reflective support.

articles.title: Malachy Postlethwayt on slave trade and the prospects of the British Empire in Africa
articles.authors: Ana Paula Londe Silva
articles.abstract: Malachy Postlethwayt, former director and propagandist of the Royal African Company, was an authority on commercial matters among Anglo-American abolitionists. The author’s unique journey would be appealing to the antislavery cause. In less than a decade, Postlethwayt shifted from offering an apologetic defense of the transatlantic slave trade to arguing that it could hinder the development of a civilized, humane, and profitable commerce in African commodities and staple crops. Over the next decades, the author became the recognized source for an important argument for abolition: the commodity trade with African territories could be at least as profitable as the slave trade. This article reappraises the historical context of Postlethwayt’s publications in the 1740s and early 1750s to demonstrate how the argument for a legitimate commerce with Africa arose amid mid-eighteenth-century debates about the fate of the Royal African Company.

articles.title: Urban–Rural Gaps in Household Living Conditions in Nepal: Evidence from the 2022 Nepal Demographic and Health Survey
articles.authors: Porokmi Sambahamphe
articles.abstract: In 2022, 94 percent of rural Nepali households had electricity, while 21 percent used a clean main cooking fuel. Using 13,786 households from the 2022 Nepal Demographic and Health Survey, I compare nine living conditions across urban and rural municipalities. The largest urban advantages are in clean cooking fuel, finished floors, and finished walls. After adjusting for geography, household assets, and household-head characteristics, the gaps are 18, 15, and 13 percentage points. For housing materials and crowding, the estimated urban gap is 0.357 index points with an asset measure that excludes the outcomes. Adding the three building-material indicators to that measure lowers the estimate to 0.122. Nearly half of the households lacking clean cooking fuel, a finished floor, and finished walls live in urban municipalities. A rural-only rule would reach 51 percent of these households, while a rule based on missing at least one basic service would reach 41 percent.

articles.title: “Ascending dragon or blasting the dragon vein?”: Contesting corporate environmental legitimacy in digital public
articles.authors: Yingnian Tao; Mark Ryan
articles.abstract: Corporations’ sustainability communication is increasingly challenged by digital publics. This study examines how Chinese netizens discursively delegitimise a controversial fireworks display staged in the Himalayas by international mountaineering brand Arc’teryx. Comments from seven popular Weibo posts (140,584 tokens) were examined through corpus-assisted discourse analysis, using keyword and concordance analysis. Findings show that netizens mobilised ecological reasoning to challenge corporate environmental reassurances, invoked environmental regulations to question perceived inequalities in enforcement, and drew on spiritual-cultural values and nationalism to condemn the display. Emotional criticism and calls for boycotts further challenged the brand, the artist, and local government authorities. These discursive resources provided distinct but overlapping grounds for evaluating environmental responsibility and demonstrate the interdependence of the human-nature relationship that Weibo netizens hold. The study demonstrates that corporate environmental legitimacy is contested not only through assessment of ecological impacts but also through broader institutional, moral, and cultural expectations.

articles.title: When the Melting Pot Becomes a Stressor: Changes in Racial Composition and Psychological Distress among Non-Hispanic Whites
articles.authors: Pui Yin Cheung; David Stuart Curtis; Ming Wen
articles.abstract: Residential diversity has risen across the United States, yet its implications for the mental health of Whites, the dominant racial group, remain poorly understood. Integrating racial threat theory, the ideologies of whiteness, and the stress process model, we ask (1) whether declining neighborhood White presence and the presence of specific racial/ethnic groups are associated with psychological distress, and (2) whether perceived neighborhood disorder and distrust, physical decay, social integration, and discrimination explain these associations. Analyzing three waves of the Midlife in the United States study (11,772 person-waves) with person fixed effects and inverse-probability-of-censoring weights, we find that declines in White proportion, and increases in Hispanic presence, are associated with greater distress. Disorder and distrust (18.5%) and social integration (13.1%) mediate the White-proportion association; disorder also mediates Black and Hispanic associations, whereas decay and discrimination do not. Demographic change thus becomes race-neutral distress for the dominant group.

articles.title: Shaping Women’s Fortunes: Inheritance and Gender Disparities
articles.authors: Naomi Crowther; Louisa Roos; Carolyn Fisher
articles.abstract: Women rely on intra- and inter-generational transfers for wealth accumulation more than men, yet the role of inheritance in closing gender wealth gaps remains poorly understood. Using Swedish registry inheritance data from 2002–2004 combined with panel data on individual wealth portfolios and labor income from 1999–2007, we examine how wealth and income evolve upon inheriting. Inheritance leads to larger relative increases in women’s net wealth compared to men, however the difference disappears in the long term. Differences in portfolio composition as well as unequal inheritance of productive assets, in the form of business ownership, may play a role. We find evidence indicative of structural barriers to financial resource accumulation over the lifecycle rather than inherent gender differences in investment preferences. The disparity in wealth accumulation post-inheritance is reinforced by gendered labor supply responses. Daughters reduce their paid labor supply more than sons, seemingly to provide unpaid eldercare. Given these findings, inheritance alone should not be viewed as an effective mechanism for reducing gender wealth inequality. (Stone Center on Socio-Economic Inequality Working Paper)

articles.title: Beyond Parental Leave: Childcare Access and Research Participation in Higher Education
articles.authors: Rachel-Ann Jones
articles.abstract: Childcare and caring responsibilities can shape researchers’ ability to participate in higher education beyond periods of parental leave, yet policy support often concentrates on career interruptions or additional costs associated with specific activities. This structured narrative review synthesises evidence from academic career research, wider labour-market studies and UK research policy to examine how caregiving demands and access to childcare may relate to research participation, progression and retention. The evidence suggests that parental status alone is an inadequate indicator of constraint: caregiving intensity, predictability and access to affordable, reliable replacement care are relevant to protected research time and mobility. Drawing on these findings, the review proposes an evidence-informed participation framework linking time and mobility constraints with access to career-building opportunities, research continuity and potential longer-term career outcomes. A mapping of UK policy distinguishes support for defined interruptions and activity-specific caring costs from provision for routine childcare. Direct evidence on the long-term effects of childcare affordability and the effectiveness of interventions in research careers remains limited. The framework therefore identifies testable mechanisms and priorities for evaluating how higher education institutions and research funders support sustained research participation.

articles.title: Diverse Paths After First Birth: Maternal Employment Trajectories in Hungary, East Germany, and West Germany, 1991–2012
articles.authors: Lili Vargha; Antonino Polizzi; Anette Eva Fasang
articles.abstract: East Germany shares a socialist legacy of full-time maternal employment with Hungary and, since 1990, a family-policy framework with West Germany. Did these shared conditions lead to similar maternal employment pathways after first birth? Comparing these contexts requires following mothers longitudinally, capturing the diversity of their pathways, their employment intensity and stability, and separating them by subsequent childbearing, which can prolong interruptions and differs across contexts. Using panel data on first births in 1991–2012, we apply group-based multi-trajectory models and bias-adjusted regressions to six years of monthly employment, separately for mothers with one child and mothers with additional children. In both groups, Hungarian mothers were concentrated in one dominant pathway, whereas German mothers spread across several. Among one-child mothers, no or very late return became similarly uncommon across contexts by 2007–2012, but mothers returned through different pathways: late full-time in Hungary, part-time in West Germany, and mixed pathways in East Germany. Among mothers with additional children, no return within six years remained at two thirds in Hungary but fell to about one fifth in both German contexts, first in the East and then in the West. East-West differences in employment intensity persisted and were larger among mothers with additional children.

articles.title: Who Speaks in the News?  Measuring Voice through Automated Quote Extraction.
articles.authors: Emma Bonutti D'Agostini; Etienne Ollion; Guilhem Sicard
articles.abstract: Quotes are central to journalism and a valuable resource for media analysis. Yet, they remain underexplored in large-scale empirical research, due to challenges in automatic extraction. We argue that quotes offer valuable opportunities to revisit core questions on the mediated public sphere – provided an extraction strategy exists that measures up to concrete social science research problems. To this end, we introduce QED (Quote Erat Detectendum), a lightweight, open-source, multilingual tool that comprehensively identifies direct, mixed and indirect reported speech triplets – composed of a source, a statement, and a cue – and attributes them to speakers. QED vastly improves on classic techniques and outperforms generative LLMs in flexibility, granularity, and scalability. Applying QED to French political news, we demonstrate its analytical value for contemporary social scientists via three illustrations in political sociology, analyzing the voice of political actors in news content.

articles.title: Mostly schooling and rurality: why older adults' internet access tracks fixed broadband across Chilean municipalities, 2013 to 2024
articles.authors: Manuel Torres-Sahli
articles.abstract: Older people's internet access varies between places. These gaps between places can be read in two ways: as reflecting features of the places, such as their infrastructure, or characteristics of the people who live there, such as their schooling and income. In Chile, the share of people aged 60 and over with internet at home rose from 41% to 92% between 2013 and 2024, mostly through phones. The share is higher in municipalities with more fixed broadband subscriptions per household. We ask how much of the gap in access between municipalities with more and fewer subscriptions reflects the older people who live in them. For 331 municipalities, we link five waves of the national household survey to the regulator's subscription counts, comparing municipalities with each other and over time. Once the older population's schooling, income, age, sex and rural residence are held constant, 62% to 85% of this gap disappears, mostly through schooling and rural residence. Measured infrastructure (antenna density and download speeds) accounts for 8% to 17% of the gap. Much of that 8% to 17% overlaps with rural residence. Over time, access rose little or no faster in municipalities where subscriptions grew faster. Most of the gap therefore reflects the older people who live in each municipality. Rural residence describes the place as well, since rural areas cost more to connect. Chile's national policy puts infrastructure first, and the findings fit pairing networks with skills and support that let older adults use them when they choose to.

articles.title: Os três corpos de uma eleição: Eleitorado, candidaturas e eleitos no Brasil (1998–2026)
articles.authors: Vitor de Moraes Peixoto
articles.abstract:
O eleitorado brasileiro feminizou-se, envelheceu e escolarizou-se em duas décadas. Este artigo
pergunta o que aconteceu com os outros dois corpos de uma eleição, o de quem se apresenta e o de
quem é escolhido, medindo duas distâncias, a das candidaturas até a população e a dos eleitos até as
candidaturas, em cinco dimensões sociográficas e uma sexta, de trajetória política, nas quinze eleições
de 1998 a 2026, sobre o universo de 3,2 milhões de registros do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral. Toda
série é calculada dentro de um de seis grupos de cargos, e não por tipo de eleição, porque cada tipo é
dominado por um cargo só. O resultado central é que as duas distâncias não se movem no mesmo
sentido: no gênero, nos seis grupos de cargos sem exceção, a distância até o eleitorado encolheu e o
filtro da urna cresceu, e nos três grupos de eleição proporcional, que reúnem mais de nove em cada
dez candidaturas do país, a urna absorveu entre metade e três quartos do que o registro fechou. Na
escolaridade e na classe ocupacional a distância persiste, disfarçada pelo crescimento do denominador
populacional; na cor, nenhuma das duas se move. A dimensão que mais separa registro de mandato
é a trajetória política: metade dos assentos legislativos vai a quem tenta a reeleição, e a fração de
estreantes cai ao mínimo da série em 2026.

articles.title: A Forgotten Chapter of Migrant Democracy: TISBO's Pioneering Political Participation Project for Older Turkish Migrants, 1994
articles.authors: Cemal YILMAZ
articles.abstract:
This article examines the pioneering political participation initiatives undertaken by the Turkish Islamic Elderly Union (Turks-Islamitische Ouderen Bond, TISBO) in the Netherlands in 1994. At a time when older migrants were frequently discussed in relation to welfare provision, social dependency and care needs, TISBO promoted a forward-looking approach that recognised older Turkish migrants as active participants in democratic and civic life. 

Employing a qualitative historical case-study design, the research draws on original organisational correspondence, meeting programmes, prepared political speeches, provincial government documents and contemporary administrative records. Particular attention is devoted to political information programmes organised in cooperation with provincial authorities in North Holland and South Holland in January 1994. The archival evidence documents TISBO's efforts to bring older Turkish migrants into direct contact with elected representatives and political parties, explain the Dutch political and electoral system, provide Turkish-language information and encourage participation in public affairs. The involvement of representatives from different political parties demonstrates the pluralistic orientation of these initiatives, while cooperation with provincial institutions illustrates the organisation's capacity to establish connections between migrant communities and formal democratic structures. 

The study distinguishes documented organisational activities from intended outcomes and avoids assuming measurable changes in electoral participation without supporting evidence. It argues that TISBO's initiatives represented an early migrant-led approach to civic inclusion that extended beyond conventional welfare-oriented perspectives on older migrants. The findings contribute to the historical understanding of migrant ageing, political participation and civil society representation in the Netherlands.

articles.title: Mapping the Digital Public Organisation: Adapting Kevin Lynch’s Methods to Digital Tool Imageability in a Local Authority
articles.authors: David Batchelor; Jennifer Schooling
articles.abstract: Digital transformation is altering the socio-technical experience of working within organisations. Software, platforms, and artificial intelligence systems have become the legible features of the workplace geography in which individuals operate. This technical note details a novel research methodology that translates methods from Kevin Lynch’s seminal work The Image of the City into an organisational context. It aims to illuminate a methodology for investigating how individuals perceive their socio-technical workplace. It engages public-sector development management planners and digital transformation officers in forming the methodology. The technical note presents the methodology, example research artefacts, and a discussion on its approach and expansion.

articles.authors: Manuel Torres-Sahli
articles.abstract: Older people's internet access varies between places. Once the older population's schooling, income, age, sex and rural residence are held constant, 62% to 85% of this gap disappears, mostly through schooling and rural residence.
